independent_solution: i + j has components (1, 1): magnitude sqrt(1+1) = sqrt2, tan(theta) = 1 -> 45 deg with the x-axis. i - j has components (1, -1): magnitude sqrt2 at -45 deg with the x-axis.
Unit vectors along them: n1 = (i+j)/sqrt2, n2 = (i-j)/sqrt2 (perpendicular). Component of A = 2i + 3j along n1 = A.n1 = (2+3)/sqrt2 = 5/sqrt2; along n2 = A.n2 = (2-3)/sqrt2 = -1/sqrt2.
questions.independent_answer: |i+j| = sqrt2 at 45 deg; |i-j| = sqrt2 at -45 deg with the x-axis; components of A: 5/sqrt2 along i+j and -1/sqrt2 along i-j.
questions.official_answer: 45 deg with the x-axis for i+j (magnitude sqrt2); -45 deg with the x-axis for i-j (magnitude sqrt2); components 5/sqrt2 and -1/sqrt2.

independent_solution: Full stem and Fig. 4.1 read on pinned pages 1-2: u = a i + b j is drawn from O up and to the right; v starts at the head of u and points down and slightly to the right.
u in the first quadrant direction -> a > 0, b > 0; v points right and down -> p > 0, q < 0.
Only option (b) 'a, p and b are positive while q is negative' fits.
r_x = r cos(theta), theta measured from the +X axis, with |r| fixed.
cos(theta) is largest (= 1) at theta = 0; along +/-Y r_x = 0; at 45 deg r_x = r/sqrt2 < r. So maximum when r is along +X.
